title: Comparison card paints growth from zero as +100% that what-changed refuses
body:
## Summary
MetricDeltaCard computes a percentage from a zero base and shows +100%, while generateWhatChanged - the other implementation of the same comparison - refuses a zero base.

## Description
`pctChange(0, n)` hardcodes 100 (src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/comparisonHelpers.ts:14). `generateWhatChanged` only computes a token/cost percentage when both sides are > 0 (:91, :101); `MetricDeltaCard` only guards null (src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/ComparisonMetrics.tsx:33). So 0 -> 4000 tokens prints "+100%" with an amber TrendingUp in the card directly under a what-changed list that says nothing. The card's own comment (:27-32) records the same defect fixed once for the null case. Fixed = growth from a zero base renders the em dash, like an unmeasured side; 0 -> 0 stays 0%.

## Flow
- compare a run that failed before calling the model (0 tokens, $0) with one that completed
- Input tokens card shows 0 -> 4.0k and +100% in amber
- the what-changed list above shows no token change

## Expected impact
The comparison stops inventing a percentage the summary refuses. Could break: nothing - 0 -> 0 and non-zero bases are pinned by the existing test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for a zero base on both comparison surfaces
Before: 1 of 2 surfaces computes a % from a zero base (card shows +100%) - vitest red
After: 0 of 2 (re-measured at build)
Method: gate - red test comparisonMetricZeroBase.test.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/comparisonHelpers.ts:13-16 pctChange: if (a === 0) return b === 0 ? 0 : 100;
src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/comparisonHelpers.ts:89-91 generateWhatChanged guards totalLeft > 0 && totalRight > 0
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/ComparisonMetrics.tsx:33-34 measured = both non-null; pct = pctChange(leftVal, rightVal)
vitest comparisonMetricZeroBase: "+100%" rendered for 0 -> 4000
impact_why: A run that failed before its first model call reads as a +100% token or cost regression in amber - an invented figure.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)

title: Annotation editor's tag field, note field and add button have no accessible name
body:
## Summary
The tag input and note textarea carry their caption in an unassociated span, and the add-tag button is a bare icon, so none has an accessible name.

## Description
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/AnnotationEditor.tsx:112-114 and :173-175 render captions as plain spans; the controls at :132 and :176 have only placeholders; the add button at :147-154 has no name. Fixed = aria-label from the existing annotation_tags_label / annotation_note_label keys and common.add for the button; no new strings. The hardcoded "Remove {tag}" label (:126) needs a new key and is left for the copy pass.

## Flow
- open an execution detail, Annotations aside
- tab through it with a screen reader
- hear "edit text", "button", "edit text multi line"

## Expected impact
The fields and button are named. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every control in the editor has an accessible name
Before: 3 nameless controls - vitest red
After: 0 of those 3 (re-measured at build)
Method: gate - red test annotationEditorA11y.test.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A cut-off or cancelled re-run reads "Running..." forever under "Cohort complete"
body:
## Summary
Rows that were cut off by the wait budget, cancelled in flight, or never dispatched keep status running/pending after the cohort phase is completed, so the report says "Running..." indefinitely and the strip says "Cohort complete".

## Description
BulkRunStatus has no terminal class for "we stopped watching" (src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:40). A null landing returns early leaving 'running' (:261); cancel flips phase to completed (:325) leaving queued rows 'pending'. The report maps both to "Running..." (src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/BulkRerunReport.tsx:220) and the strip announces completion (src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/BulkRerunStrip.tsx:33). Registry: fleet-orchestration / result-harvest ("classify every member of the roster into a terminal account"). Fixed = 'timed_out' and 'cancelled' item statuses, counted in the cohort, labelled in report and strip.

## Flow
- confirm a cohort; cancel after 2 of 6
- strip: "Cohort complete - 1/6 succeeded"
- report: 4 rows "Running..." that will never update

## Expected impact
The report accounts for every member. Could break: the existing pin item.status toBe('running') (useBulkRerun.test.ts:212) is rewritten; 3 surfaces change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every cohort member ends in a terminal, labelled state
Before: cut-off/cancelled members: 0 terminal states (code read + existing test pins running)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - walked deadline, cancel-in-flight, cancel-before-dispatch; the instrument is S but the change spans hook + 2 views + copy (M, risk 4)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:40 BulkRunStatus = 'pending' | 'running' | 'success' | 'failed' (no cut-off class)
src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:261 if (!landed) return; // comment: "stays pending" - status is 'running' (:236)
src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:325 cancel(): setPhase('completed')
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/BulkRerunReport.tsx:220 pending|running -> e.running_state
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/BulkRerunStrip.tsx:33 bulk_rerun_strip_done = "Cohort complete - {success}/{total} succeeded"
impact_why: After the 15-minute wait or a cancel, nothing polls the row again, yet the report keeps claiming it is running and the strip calls the cohort complete.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)
instrument: renderHook(useBulkRerun) with pollTimeoutMs 0 and a never-landing run, then render BulkRerunReport/Strip from its state: Before row shows running_state under phase completed and strip "Cohort complete"; After the row has a terminal "not settled"/"cancelled" class and the strip says the cohort was cut short.

title: Synthetic waterfall draws stages past the end of runs shorter than ~100 ms
body:
## Summary
buildSyntheticTrace gives each estimated stage a minimum width; under ~100 ms of wall clock the minimums alone exceed the run, so spans end after completedAt.

## Description
Each stage gets `Math.max(total * pct, floor)` (src/features/agents/sub_executions/trace/SyntheticTrace.ts:60-91) and stream_output a 50 ms floor (:81). For an 80 ms run the spans sum to 90+ ms while `completedAt` stays at 80 ms, so PipelineWaterfall's bars (leftPct/widthPct over the trace span) run past 100%. Fixed = when the floored spans exceed the wall clock, scale every span proportionally into it; runs long enough to fit are untouched.

## Flow
- open a run that failed in validation after 80 ms
- the waterfall reconstructs 7 stages with floors
- the last stage ends at 90 ms on an 80 ms axis

## Expected impact
The estimated waterfall of a fast failure stays inside its own axis. Could break: nothing for runs over ~100 ms (pinned by the long-run case).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every synthetic span ends within the run
Before: 20 ms run: last span ends at 30 ms; 80 ms run: 90 ms (2 of 3 cases red)
After: 3 of 3 inside the run, 10 s run unchanged (re-measured at build)
Method: gate - red test SyntheticTrace.shortRun.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_executions/trace/SyntheticTrace.ts:60-91 per-stage floors (5,10,5,10,50,10,5 ms)
src/features/agents/sub_executions/trace/SyntheticTrace.ts:81 actualStreamDur = Math.max(streamDur, 50)
vitest: "expected 30 to be less than or equal to 20" (20 ms run), "expected 90 to be less than or equal to 80" (80 ms run)
impact_why: Fast failures (validation errors) are exactly the short runs; their estimated waterfall overflows the run and misstates every bar.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)

title: List filters search only loaded pages, so "No results" shows while matches remain
body:
## Summary
Origin, status and capability filters run client-side over the pages already loaded, and an empty filtered page shows the generic "No results" while Load more is still offered.

## Description
Filters at src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/ExecutionList.tsx:70-76 run over `paging.rows` (50 per page). The empty state (:205) does not say the search was partial. Registry: table deviation (keyset-trace-pagination: "paging a list under filters"). Fixed = push the filters to the server query, or at minimum make the empty state say how many runs were searched.

## Flow
- persona with 300 runs, latest 50 all completed
- filter status = failed
- "No results", with Load more below

## Expected impact
Filters answer the question asked. Could break: server-side filtering changes paging offsets.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a filter result covers what it claims
Before: filter covers 50 of N runs (code read)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - walked three persona sizes (30, 120, 300 runs); the real fix crosses into the paging hook and the backend
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: Filtering for failed or a capability on a persona with 300 runs says "No results" when the matches are on page 3.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)
instrument: executionListDefects harness: 50 loaded completed rows, server holds failed rows at offset 60; set status filter failed; Before shows common.no_results with Load more; After either server-filters or labels the empty state as "none in loaded N".

title: JSON diff compares top-level keys only and folds an absent key into null
body:
## Summary
jsonDiff serialises each top-level value and compares strings, so nested changes surface as one opaque key and absent-vs-null is invisible.

## Description
Registry: software-engineering/diff-comparison - semantic-level-selection and invisible-differences. src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/comparisonDiffCore.ts:84-85 (unmapped file, shared with the worker) compares at depth one with `?? null`. Fixed = recurse to leaf paths and keep absent distinct from null.

## Flow
- compare two runs whose input differs in config.retries
- Input Data Diff shows one row "config" with two long JSON blobs

## Expected impact
Diffs point at the field that changed. Could break: the worker bundle gate (comparisonWorkerGraph.test) must stay green.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the JSON diff names the changed leaf
Before: depth 1 (code read)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - three walked payloads; file is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: Two inputs differing in one nested field show the whole subtree as one changed key; {a: null} vs {} reads as identical.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)
instrument: comparisonDiffCore.test: jsonDiff('{"a":null}', '{}') and a nested-path case; Before 0 diffs / 1 coarse diff, After 1 diff / the nested path.

title: Active-chains badge shows a frozen snapshot indefinitely once polling fails
body:
## Summary
On a poll failure the badge keeps the last good list with no indication, so it can report chains in flight for as long as the IPC keeps failing.

## Description
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/ActiveChainsBadge.tsx:26-34 logs and keeps state; nothing records that the snapshot is old. The badge is the live "what is running now" signal (:13-18), so a stale answer is the failure the state-coverage lens names: a screen that renders as though nothing is wrong. Fixed = after consecutive failures, mark the list stale (or hide it) and show when it was last confirmed.

## Flow
- a chain is in flight; the badge shows 1
- the backend IPC starts failing
- the chain finishes; the badge shows 1 in flight indefinitely

## Expected impact
The badge stops asserting live state it cannot confirm. Could break: one new copy line.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed refresh is distinguishable from a confirmed state
Before: 0 stale indications after any number of failed polls (code read)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - walked transient single failure, chronic failure, recovery; needs a new English key
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/ActiveChainsBadge.tsx:26-34 catch: logger.warn; "keep last good state"
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/ActiveChainsBadge.tsx:56 renders whenever chains.length > 0
impact_why: A chain that finished while the IPC was failing keeps showing as in flight with no hint the data is stale.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)
instrument: Render the badge, first listActiveChains resolves 1 chain, then every poll rejects: Before still shows "1 chain in flight" after N polls with no stale marker; After marks it stale after 2 failures.

title: Annotation edits typed before the saved annotation loads are wiped when it lands
body:
## Summary
The reset effect overwrites local edits whenever the annotation prop changes, including the first load that lands after the user started typing.

## Description
src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/AnnotationEditor.tsx:39-43 has no dirty guard. ExecutionDetail passes `byExecution.get(id) ?? null` from an async hook, so the first render is null and the loaded annotation arrives later.

## Flow
- open an execution detail with a saved annotation
- type in the note before the annotation request resolves
- the request resolves; the note is replaced

## Expected impact
Typed drafts survive the load. Could break: a draft could hide a newer server value unless offered.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a dirty draft is not overwritten by a load
Before: draft replaced (walked)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - walked load-before-type, type-before-load, save-then-refresh
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/AnnotationEditor.tsx:39-43 useEffect resets tags/note/starred whenever annotation id/tags/note/starred change
impact_why: A fast typist on a slow load loses the tag or note they started.
predicted_why: like 9df2764add (git, decision memory empty), accepted: "background refresh no longer overwrites an edit"
instrument: Render with annotation=null, type a note, rerender with a loaded annotation: Before the note is replaced; After a dirty draft is kept (and the loaded value offered).

title: Bulk re-run idempotency key embeds Date.now(), so it can never deduplicate
body:
## Summary
Each dispatch mints a key containing the current millisecond, so a re-dispatch of the same original in the same cohort can never collide with the first.

## Description
Registry: fleet-orchestration (deviation recorded 2026-10-21). src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:245. Today nothing retries a dispatch, so the key is inert rather than harmful; a key derived from (cohort id, original id) would make a retried dispatch safe.

## Flow
- a dispatch times out in IPC while the backend enqueued it
- any retry would enqueue a second run

## Expected impact
Only matters once a retry path exists. Could break: a cohort re-run of the same original inside the backend dedupe window would be deduplicated.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a retried dispatch is deduplicated
Before: key unique per call (code read)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - no retry path exists to exercise
Result: better
Gate: none
impact_why: The key exists to make a repeated dispatch safe; minted fresh per call it never matches a prior one.
predicted_why: no precedent (door decisions empty; none in cycle-1 git)
instrument: Two confirms of the same cohort row within the dedupe window: count backend executions created (Before 2).
